description: Returning user (seed R01, Maria, 48, perimenopausal, on HRT), docs/ux/F02c › Returning. Unlike the first consult, Deborah opens from memory: welcome back, how last time's plan went, a sleep score, then the new concern. She never re-asks the profile: safety check first, 4 new questions (one free text), then Maria decides when to see the 7-section answer. Ends with booking and a check-in.
contentStatus: DRAFT. All Deborah-voice copy, tests and product guidance need Deborah's clinical sign-off before any user-facing use.

welcome_back.bot: Welcome back, Maria. How have you been since we last talked?

plan_check.bot: Last time we talked about your night sweats and broken sleep. Did the changes help at all? The cooler bedroom, an earlier dinner, and morning light.

plan_good.bot: I'm so glad. Even a little better is your body responding, and that tells us something.

plan_ack.bot: Thank you for being honest. Small changes take a few weeks to show, so none of that is wasted.

sleep_score.bot: Quick one so I can track it over time: how would you rate your sleep this week?

memory.bot: I'll keep that next to last time's score. I still have your estradiol patch and progesterone on file, and the heavy days you mentioned, so we don't need to go over any of that again.

whats_new.bot: So, what's on your mind today?

user_open.user: I keep waking at 2am with my heart fluttering.

safety_q.bot: Oh, I'm sorry, Maria. Waking at 2am with your heart fluttering is unsettling, especially when you're already short on sleep. One quick safety check first: when it happens, do you ever have chest pain or pressure, trouble breathing, or feel like you might faint?
safety_q.uiNote: Always first for heart symptoms. 'Yes' shows the F03 emergency card, stops the consultation and never counts toward the free limit.

emergency.bot: Chest pain, trouble breathing or feeling faint with a racing heart needs care right now, not a chat. If it's happening now, call 911.

after_emergency.bot: I'm glad you're safe right now, Maria. Please have this checked by a provider soon. This conversation doesn't count toward your free answers.

q_duration.bot: Good. How long does an episode last, and does it come with a wave of heat or sweat? You mentioned night sweats in your profile, so I want to see if they're linked.
q_duration.uiNote: Uses her symptom checklist instead of asking about night sweats again.

q_onset.bot: When did this start? You've been on your estradiol patch and progesterone for about a year. Did the flutters begin around a dose change, on patch-change days, or on their own?
q_onset.uiNote: Uses her HRT detail fields. Deborah never asks 'Are you on any medication?'

options.label: Not linked that I can tell

q_evening.bot: What do your evenings usually look like after 7pm? For example, dinner time, wine, sweets, or screens.
q_evening.uiNote: The only free-text question: the profile captures diet in general, not her evening routine.

widget.placeholder: e.g. dinner at 8, a glass of wine…

q_iron.bot: Last one. Your profile notes some heavy days, around 7 pads at their peak. Have you had your iron or ferritin checked in the past year?
q_iron.uiNote: Turns an old reproductive-history answer into a lead: heavy bleeding can deplete iron, and low iron can contribute to palpitations.

ready.bot: Thank you, that's what I need. Do you want my findings now, or is there anything you'd like to add first?

add_more.bot: Of course. What would you like me to know?

thinking.bot: Looking at this through Deborah's upstream lens…

sections.title: What I'm Hearing
sections.body: Maria, you're 48, in perimenopause and about a year into HRT. Around 2am you wake drenched, with a brief flutter in your chest, on very little sleep and a lot of stress. That's exhausting, and it makes sense it's worrying you.

sections.title: The Hypothalamic Connection
sections.body: Your hypothalamus runs your thermostat, your sleep and your stress response. Shifting hormones in perimenopause can unsettle all three at once, and a 2am wake-up often comes with a stress-hormone surge you may feel as your heart racing.

sections.title: What This May Mean
body: Hormone swings that your current HRT timing may not cover overnight are worth exploring.
A blood sugar dip after evening wine may play a part.
Heavy days may have lowered your iron, which can contribute to a fluttering heart.
Thyroid function is worth a fresh look.

sections.title: Questions for Your Provider
body: Could my HRT dose or timing be adjusted for my night sweats?
Could my heavy periods have lowered my iron?
Should I have an ECG or a heart rhythm monitor to rule out an arrhythmia?
Is my progesterone timed well for sleep?

body.why: Checks whether heavy days have depleted your iron.

body.test: Full thyroid panel with free T3
body.why: Looks beyond TSH at how your thyroid is really working.
Shows whether blood sugar dips could be waking you.
Rules out a heart rhythm problem.

sections.title: What You Can Do Now
body: Try pausing evening wine for two weeks and notice your nights.
Have a small protein snack before bed to keep blood sugar steady.
Keep your bedroom cool and dark.
Log each episode in Visit Notes: time, how long, and what came before.

productCard.name: Genesis Gold®
productCard.line: Plant-based nutrition designed to support the hypothalamus. Most women give it at least 90 days.
productCard.personalNote: You're on HRT, so check with your prescriber before starting.

sections.title: A Word from Deborah
sections.body: Maria, a fluttering heart at 2am is frightening, and you were right to bring it up. Let's rule out the serious causes first, then work with your hormones, not against them.

answer.footer: Bring this to your provider. I help you ask better questions — your provider makes clinical decisions.

ask_weight.uiNote: Weight is asked only here, at the product, never during intake.

weight.bot: What's your weight? Pounds or kilograms are both fine.

offer_booking.bot: Because the flutters are new, I'd really like to hear about them myself. Here are my next openings, if you'd like one.

confirm_booking.bot: Lovely. Just check this looks right.
confirm_booking.uiNote: Price is placeholder; no payment, simulated.

booked.bot: You're booked. Bring your flutter notes if you can: what time, how long, and what you'd eaten.

offer_checkin.bot: Shall I check in next week to see whether the 2am wake-ups have eased?

close.bot: Take care of yourself tonight, Maria. I'm right here if anything changes.
